newsitem.title: TURKEY: Islamist charity faces closure by Turkish court.
newsitem.headline: Islamist charity faces closure by Turkish court.

text.p: A Turkish court on Thursday began the trial of an Islamist charity facing closure over its alleged financial support for outlawed religious groups, Anatolian news agency said.
The prosecutor asked for jail sentences of a maximum seven years and six months for each of the Unity Foundation's five directors in a hearing at the Ankara state security court.

The defendants were charged in June with providing financial aid to jailed religious activists and armed Islamist groups, including the Great Islamic Eastern Raiders-Front (IBDA-C) and the Turkish Hizbullah, unrelated to the similarly named group in Lebanon.
The case begun amid a secularist crackdown on religious activism initiated by the powerful military in the course of a row with the former Islamist-led government.
Turkey's first Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned last month as prime minister as the row intensified.
Anatolian quoted the indictment as saying the foundation supported activities against the state, covering its work as providing aid to imprisoned people.
The accused all appeared in court and denied the charges. The prosecutor also demanded the foundation be closed and its assests be seized, the agency said.
